Fertilizer for paddy – the DOA way:
• Basal: mix TSP and MOP into the mud at the last ploughing, before sowing.
• Urea in split doses: about 2 weeks, 4 weeks and at panicle start (about 6–7 weeks for a 3½-month variety). Never all at once.
• Apply urea onto 2–3 cm of water, then close the field inlets and outlets for 3–4 days. Don't apply before heavy rain.
• Dark green leaves with blast or brown planthopper around? Stop extra urea.
• Use the amounts in the DOA fertilizer recommendation for your variety's age. Adding compost or ploughing in straw lets you use less.
• My Crop builds the exact dates for your field.

Water for paddy:
• First 3–4 days: keep the soil just wet, no standing water, so the seedlings root well. Then keep 2–5 cm.
• Tillering: keep 2–5 cm of water. A 5–7 day drain in mid-tillering makes roots strong and saves water.
• Panicle start to flowering: never let the field dry – keep about 5 cm. Shortage now gives empty grains.
• Ripening: keep the soil wet, then drain 10–14 days before harvest.
• Short of water? Alternate wetting and drying: let the water drop until the soil shows fine cracks, then fill again (not during flowering).

Weed control in paddy:
• Level the field well and keep 2–5 cm of water after the seedlings are up – water stops most weeds.
• Use clean seed paddy with no weed seeds.
• Weedicide: EITHER a pre-emergence weedicide 0–4 days after sowing on moist soil, OR a post-emergence weedicide at 6–10 days when the weeds have 1–3 leaves. Pick one labelled for paddy and for your weeds (grasses, sedges or broad-leaf), and use the label dose.
• Hand weed or use a rotary weeder at about 2 and 4 weeks – the first 30–40 days decide the yield.
• Weedy rice (shatters early, red grain): plough once, let the weeds sprout for 1–2 weeks with water, then plough again before sowing.

Weedicides by days after sowing:
• 2 days before sowing – Sofit (for weedy rice)
• Day 0–4 – Sofit
• Day 6–10 – Solito 320 EC or Profit 500 EC
• Day 8–15 – Facet Quinclorac (Maruk)
• Day 21–28 – MCPA 60 (sedges and broad-leaf weeds)

நெல்வயலில் களைக் கட்டுப்பாடு:
• வயலை நன்கு சமன் செய்து, நாற்றுகள் வந்தபின் 2–5 செ.மீ. நீர் வையுங்கள் – நீர் பெரும்பாலான களைகளைத் தடுக்கும்.
• களை விதை இல்லாத சுத்தமான விதைநெல்லைப் பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.

Seed paddy and sowing:
• Use certified seed or your own clean, well-dried seed of a recommended variety.
• Salt-water test: put seed in salt water strong enough to float an egg and remove the seeds that float.
• Soak 24 hours, then keep covered in a damp sack for about 48 hours until the sprouts are 2–3 mm.
• Seed rate: about 100 kg per hectare (40 kg per acre) for broadcasting; about half that for transplanting or parachute seedlings.
• Sow on a well-levelled, puddled field with a thin film of water so seeds don't rot in pools.
• Sow at the same time as your neighbours – it reduces pests, birds and rats.

Land preparation:
• Repair the bunds and clean the channels first.
• First ploughing with water 3–4 weeks before sowing, so stubble and weeds rot.
• Second ploughing 1–2 weeks later kills the weeds that have sprouted.
• Final puddling and careful levelling just before sowing – a level field needs less water and has fewer weeds.
• Mix the basal fertilizer (TSP + MOP) and compost into the mud at the final puddling.

Harvesting:
• Harvest when 80–85% of the grains on the panicle are golden – about 30 days after flowering.
• Drain the field 10–14 days before harvest so the soil is firm.
• Harvesting late makes grains fall and break in the mill.
• Thresh soon after cutting. Dry the grain on mats or tarpaulin (not on the road) to 14% moisture – a dry grain cracks sharply between your teeth.
• Don't heap wet paddy overnight; it heats up and spoils.

Storing paddy:
• Store only grain dried to 14% moisture.
• Use clean, dry bags on wooden pallets, 30 cm away from the walls.
• Make the store rat-proof and set traps around it.
• Keep seed paddy separate, labelled with the variety and season, and test germination before sowing.
• Check every 2 weeks – warm or smelly bags mean moisture or insects; dry them again in the sun.

• Don't burn straw – plough it back in 3–4 weeks before sowing. It returns potassium and feeds the soil.
• Add about 5 tonnes per hectare of compost or cattle manure at land preparation.
• Gliricidia leaves as green manure: spread and plough in 2–3 weeks before sowing.
• Organic matter lets you cut chemical fertilizer, but for a high yield still give urea in split doses.

Yellow leaves – find the cause:
• Whole plants pale yellow, older leaves first → nitrogen shortage. Give the next urea dose now.
• Yellow-orange from the leaf tip, short plants in patches → tungro (virus spread by green leafhopper). Pull out sick plants and control the leafhoppers.
• Bronze/orange-brown leaves, oily orange water, low-lying field → iron toxicity. Drain and dry the field 3–5 days and add MOP.
• Round patches drying from the base, small brown insects at the base → brown planthopper. Drain the field and stop extra urea.
• Wavy yellow-white stripes from the leaf edge → bacterial leaf blight.
• Take a clear photo of one leaf with Scan to check.

• இலை நுனியிலிருந்து மஞ்சள்-செம்மஞ்சள், திட்டுகளாகக் குட்டையான பயிர் → துங்ரோ (பச்சைத் தத்துப்பூச்சி பரப்பும் வைரஸ்). நோயுற்ற பயிர்களைப் பிடுங்கித் தத்துப்பூச்சியைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துங்கள்.
• செம்பு/செம்மஞ்சள்-பழுப்பு இலைகள், எண்ணெய் போன்ற செம்மஞ்சள் நீர், தாழ்வான வயல் → இரும்பு நச்சு. 3–5 நாள் நீரை வடித்து உலர்த்தி MOP இடுங்கள்.

• இலை ஓரத்திலிருந்து அலை போன்ற மஞ்சள்-வெள்ளைக் கோடுகள் → பாக்டீரியா இலைக் கருகல்.

Spots or disease on the leaves:
• Diamond-shaped spots with a grey centre and brown edge → blast.
• Small round brown spots like sesame seeds → brown spot (often weak or poor soil).
• Yellow-white wavy stripes from the leaf edge → bacterial leaf blight.
• Grey-green oval patches on the stem near the water → sheath blight.
• Yellow-orange stunted plants in patches → tungro.
• Orange spots with red stripes running up to the leaf tip → red stripe.
• Best: take a photo of one sick leaf with Scan – AgriCare will name the disease and give the full treatment plan with alarms.

Insects in the field – match what you see:
• Round patches drying from the base, brown insects at the base → brown planthopper.
• Dead centre shoots or white empty panicles → yellow stem borer.
• Leaves folded lengthwise with white streaks → leaf folder.
• Pale hollow onion-like shoots → gall midge.
• Empty or spotted grains, bad smell → paddy bug.
• Rolled, silvery leaf tips in young dry fields → thrips.
• Count before you spray: many sprays kill the spiders that eat these pests. The Pests page has the full plan for each one.

Salty (saline) fields:
• Before sowing, let fresh water in and drain it out 2–3 times to wash the salt away.
• Grow At 354 – the DOA salt-tolerant variety.
• Use a little more seed, or transplant older (3–4 week) seedlings, which handle salt better.
• Give enough MOP (potassium) and add compost or straw; on hard sodic soil apply gypsum.
• Keep water in the field – letting it dry brings the salt up.

Iron toxicity (low-lying bog fields):
• Signs: bronze/orange-brown leaves starting from the tips, an oily orange film on the water, few dark roots, poor tillering.
• Drain the field for 3–5 days in mid-tillering to let air into the soil, then refill. Don't keep stagnant water.
• Give enough MOP (potassium) and add compost; potassium helps the roots resist iron.
• Clean the drains so water moves through the field.
• Grow Bw 367 or Bw 361, the DOA varieties for these soils.

Spraying safely and well:
• Spray in the early morning or late evening, with light wind and no rain expected for 4–6 hours (see the Weather page for a good spray day).
• Measure the dose from the label exactly – more is not better. Don't mix different chemicals in one tank.
• Wear gloves, a mask, long sleeves and boots. Don't eat, drink or smoke while spraying; wash well afterwards.
• Aim the spray where the pest is (the base of the plants for planthoppers).
• Keep children and animals away. Rinse empty bottles 3 times, pierce and bury them – never reuse.
• Keep the waiting days before harvest written on the label.

Dry season / water shortage:
• Sow only the area your water can cover till harvest.
• Choose a short variety: Bg 250 (about 85 days) or Bg 300 (about 3 months).
• Level the field well and repair the bunds – leaking bunds lose more water than the crop uses.
• Use alternate wetting and drying in tillering.
• Save your water for panicle start to flowering – that is when shortage hurts the yield most.

After heavy rain or flooding:
• Open the drains and get the water out as fast as you can – the tips of the leaves must come above the water.
• Don't put urea until the water has gone down; then give the next dose.
• In the week after the flood, check for bacterial leaf blight and blast – they spread after storms.
• If young plants were under water for more than a week and most died, re-sow with a short variety such as Bg 250.
• Watch rats – they move into fields after floods.

To get a higher yield:
• Grow a recommended variety for your district and season, from clean seed.
• Level the field well – it saves water and stops weeds.
• Control weeds in the first 30–40 days.
• Give urea in split doses on time, not all at once.
• Keep water from panicle start to flowering.
• Check the field every week and act early on pests and diseases – scan a leaf when you see spots.
• Harvest on time and dry the grain well.

• ස්කෑන් කිරීමෙන් පසු (හෝ පළිබෝධ පිටුවක) "ප්‍රතිකාරය අරඹන්න" ඔබන්න – පියවර දින සමඟ "නිරීක්ෂණය" වෙත යයි.
• "නිරීක්ෂණය" හි "එලාම් සක්‍රිය කරන්න" ඔබා AgriCare ටැබයක විවෘතව තබන්න; පියවරක් නියමිත වූ විට එය නාද වී කතා කරයි.
• දුරකථන බ්‍රවුසරය වසා ඇති විටත් මතක් කිරීමට, සැලැස්මෙන් එක් එක් පියවර Google Calendar වෙත එක් කරන්න.

சிகிச்சை அலாரங்கள்:
• ஸ்கேன் செய்தபின் (அல்லது பூச்சிப் பக்கத்தில்) "சிகிச்சையைத் தொடங்கு" அழுத்துங்கள் – படிகள் நாட்களுடன் "கண்காணிப்பு" க்குச் செல்லும்.
• "கண்காணிப்பு" இல் "அலாரத்தை இயக்கு" அழுத்தி AgriCare ஐ ஒரு தாவலில் திறந்து வையுங்கள்; படி வரும்போது ஒலித்துப் பேசும்.
• தொலைபேசி உலாவி மூடியிருக்கும்போதும் நினைவூட்ட, திட்டத்திலிருந்து ஒவ்வொரு படியையும் Google Calendar இல் சேருங்கள்.

ඔබේ කුඹුරට කාලගුණය:
• "කාලගුණය" විවෘත කරන්න: ඔබේ ස්ථානයට හෝ දිස්ත්‍රික්කයට දින 7ක අනාවැකිය සෑම දිනකටම ගොවිතැන් උපදෙස් සමඟ පෙන්වයි – නොඉසිය යුතු හෝ යූරියා නොදැමිය යුතු දින, තද වැසි අනතුරු ඇඟවීම්, පාළුව අවදානම සහ නියං කාල.
• වැසි ඉඩ අඩු, සුළං මද දිනවල පමණක් ඉසින්න හෝ යූරියා දමන්න.

உங்கள் வயலுக்கான வானிலை:
• "வானிலை" திறவுங்கள்: உங்கள் இருப்பிடம் அல்லது மாவட்டத்துக்கான 7 நாள் முன்னறிவிப்பை ஒவ்வொரு நாளுக்கும் விவசாய ஆலோசனையுடன் காட்டும் – தெளிக்கவோ யூரியா இடவோ கூடாத நாட்கள், கனமழை எச்சரிக்கை, குலை நோய் அபாயம், வறண்ட காலம்.
• மழை வாய்ப்புக் குறைவான, காற்று மெதுவான நாட்களில் மட்டும் தெளியுங்கள் அல்லது யூரியா இடுங்கள்.
